clue.text: Good about new control

parts.note: over can mean about, as in fussing over or about something

explanation.surface: A good leader returns to manage something new.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule or direct a country or body is to have control of it.

clue.text: Italian ice cream in the wind?

definitions.meaning: a well-known brand of cone of ice cream sold in Italy and Britain
the Italian name for the cornett, a Renaissance instrument found among the wind section

explanation.surface: An ice cream cone being eaten outdoors on a breezy day.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a branded ice-cream cone and, in Italian, the old wooden cornett, a wind instrument.

clue.text: Got through old time report

indicators.note: a report is a sound heard, so the words are taken as spoken

parts.note: time gone by is the past

explanation.surface: Someone survived an old-fashioned school report.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got through an exam or a test is to have succeeded in it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Sufficient heat remaining to show where 26 may be used

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Enough warmth is left over for a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the last letter of 'Sufficient', all of 'heat' and the start of 'remaining'; 26 is BLADE, a surgeon's scalpel used in an operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: An operating theatre is where a surgeon's scalpel blade is put to use.

clue.text: Author of the 20 shows skill a little way into 10-er

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: into means the short distance goes inside the thrower word

parts.note: 10 is CHUCK, so a chucker, one who throws, is a hurler
a mil is a thousandth of an inch, a tiny distance

explanation.surface: A writer of the play displays craft by stepping a short way into a bowling crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is CRUCIBLE, the play The Crucible; 10 is CHUCK, so the '10-er' is a chucker, i.e. a hurler, which MIL splits as HUR-MIL-LER.
explanation.definitionFit: The American playwright wrote The Crucible, the 1953 drama about the Salem witch trials.

clue.text: Shiner to be interrupted by servant

indicators.note: the two letters are split apart with the servant word in the gap

parts.note: taken as written
a lackey is a footman or servant

explanation.surface: A footman barges in on someone about to become a shoeshine boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner is slang for a bruised, discoloured eye from a punch.

clue.text: Leave Mum in lake and start your verbal sparring

indicators.note: in means the departing mother goes inside the lake word

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake
to go is to leave
Ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: start means only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Instructions to abandon Mother in a lake and begin a war of words.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare word means a dispute about words, an argument conducted in words.

clue.text: Monkey in khaki for training

definitions.meaning: a West African baboon-like primate related to the mandrill
a stout twilled cotton fabric often used for khaki uniforms

explanation.surface: An ape in army uniform doing its exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'in' and 'for' are only links between the three senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a baboon species, a hard-wearing cotton cloth used for khaki, and practice by repetition.

clue.text: Shaky and seedy from start of week to the middle?

indicators.note: start of means just the opening letter of the word
shaky letters are unsteady, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling wobbly and unwell from Monday until midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaky' rearranges AND SEEDY into EDNESDAY, placed after W from 'start of week'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth day is the midpoint of the working week, hence the questioned 'the middle'.

clue.text: Throw over one's sweetheart as a bit of 8?

definitions.meaning: to jilt or abandon a lover
a northern English term of endearment, like love or dear
8 is DRILL; the clamp that holds a drill bit

explanation.surface: Dumping a lover in a scene involving a drill.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition; 'as' is a link. 8 is DRILL, and 'bit' puns on the drill bit the chuck grips.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to discard, a pet name, and the jaws on a power drill.

clue.text: Slow movement from 25 9

indicators.note: movement means the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A slow passage in a symphony comes from a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 9 is Sheffield Wednesday, an English football club whose nickname is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Sheffield Wednesday Football Club, used for its players and team.

clue.text: Loose with queasy inside needs to be put together

indicators.note: an upset stomach churns, so the inner letters are rearranged

parts.note: untied means loose, unfastened

explanation.surface: Feeling loose and sick in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the inner letters move: UNTIED becomes UN-IT-ED with its middle TI turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined into one is a straight synonym for being put together; it is also Sheffield United.

clue.text: Prize giver concerned with screw

parts.note: re means concerning or about
screw is British prison slang for a warder or jailer

explanation.surface: Someone handing out prizes is involved with a screw.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rewards somebody gives them a prize or recompense.

clue.text: Object of cocker (?) to thwart at the 20

definitions.meaning: in the phrase cock a snook, the snook is what is cocked
to block or frustrate, as by leaving an opponent no clear shot
the game played at the Crucible Theatre, Sheffield, home of its world championship

explanation.surface: A rude gesture made to obstruct someone at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is CRUCIBLE: the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the World Snooker Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the cue game, a blocking position in it, and a verb meaning to obstruct.

clue.text: As a rule, friend pursues alternative nasals

indicators.note: pursues means the friend comes after the other piece

parts.note: N or M: two nasal consonants offered as alternatives
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend chases someone speaking through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually or ordinarily, the same idiom as the phrase as a rule.

clue.text: Turning up with competence on island

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: able means having competence

explanation.surface: Arriving skilfully on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled in 1814.

clue.text: I should have written "change the book"

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is what a letter writer adds having forgotten something
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: An author regrets not writing an order to amend the volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Psalms, or a volume of psalms for worship, is a book.

clue.text: Large quantities of punishment

definitions.meaning: lots, plenty, as in ... of cream

explanation.surface: A lot of punishment being handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both abundance, chiefly British, and whippings.

clue.text: Skua from Kew has a problem

indicators.note: a problem leaves things in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A seabird from Kew Gardens is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is the botanical garden in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea hawk is an old name for the skua, a predatory gull-like seabird.

clue.text: Company with Thorndike for audience at 25 4

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a crew is a company, and Dame Sybil Thorndike was an English stage actress

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe with a famous actress performs for spectators at a Sheffield playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 4 is Sheffield theatre; 'at' is a link. Crew plus Sybil, said aloud, gives the venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible is the main theatre in Sheffield, a named example.

clue.text: Arrive by day, disheartened, to work in 4

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letter, is removed

explanation.surface: Turning up by day, feeling low, to do a job at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-hearted play is a kind of dramatic work staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Continue with employer turning to setter

indicators.note: turning means the word for employer is read backwards

parts.note: a user employs something
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: Going on after an employer turns to the crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to go on after a pause, a synonym of continue.

clue.text: Fairy in the distance raised a lottery

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the words read upwards

parts.note: an elf is a fairy creature
far means at a distance

explanation.surface: A far-off sprite lifted the prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a draw for prizes using tickets, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: See 5
Fortunate to …

parts.note: lucky, in British slang; the ellipsis runs on to the next answer, so the word is how lucky Sheffield is described

explanation.surface: A trailing remark about luck that leads into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis points to the next entry, the city of Sheffield.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammy is British slang for lucky, fortunate without deserving it.

clue.text: Attempt to muzzle Euphemia would come to the city

parts.note: sh is the sound made to hush someone
Effie is a pet form of the name Euphemia
'ld is an old contraction of would, as in I'ld

explanation.surface: Trying to silence a woman so she will come to town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is the Yorkshire city that is the theme of the puzzle.

clue.text: Boy led by his first ecstasy to be part of 25 12

indicators.note: led by means the lad comes after the other piece

parts.note: his refers to the boy, whose first letter is B
a lad is a boy
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A boy is guided by his own first experience of euphoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 12 is Sheffield United, whose players are nicknamed the Blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of Sheffield United, nicknamed the Blades after the city's cutlery trade.

clue.text: Being so disciplined, we get gold

definitions.note: describes a creature that is so, bipedal like a human

indicators.note: disciplined letters are put in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Being so well drilled, we won the medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being so' means a creature that has this feature, as people do.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipedal, walking on two legs, is how humans are as beings.
